QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_12

question.text: A Specialized Investment Fund (SIF), recently introduced by SEBI, requires a minimum investment of:

answer.text: Rs. 10 lakh per investor at PAN level across all SIF investment strategies; other mutual fund schemes are not counted
Rs. 1 crore per investor, similar to AIF Category III
Rs. 50 lakh per investor, similar to PMS
Rs. 25 lakh per investor per strategy

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 56), SEBI introduced the Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) as a new product line positioned between mutual funds and PMS, with a minimum required investment of Rs. 10 lakh across all SIF investment strategies. Page 171 clarifies that the aggregate Rs. 10 lakh threshold is measured at PAN level, and that investments in other mutual fund schemes are not counted toward this threshold. The Trap: The other options use thresholds associated with different product categories or fabricated figures, rather than the SEBI-mandated SIF minimum. Note: When recording a client's SIF eligibility, aggregate their SIF strategy investments at PAN level and exclude their other mutual fund holdings from the calculation.
